title: independent assortment probability
stem: An organism has 3 homologous chromosome pairs. Ignore crossing over and assume each pair orients independently at meiosis I. What is the chance that one gamete gets a specified maternal-or-paternal homolog from every pair, and which meiotic event creates these possible combinations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1/3; sister chromatids separate at anaphase II to create 3 equiprobable assortments.
choices.rationale: Meiosis II separates sisters; the number of whole-homolog configurations is exponential in homolog-pair count, not equal to that count.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1/8; random orientation of homologous pairs at metaphase I creates 8 equiprobable whole-chromosome assortments.
choices.rationale: Correct: Each of the 3 pairs has two independent maternal/paternal choices, giving 2^3=8 combinations and probability (1/2)^3=1/8 for one specified combination. The source of these whole-chromosome combinations is independent assortment at meiosis I; crossing over is excluded.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 1/16; random fertilization doubles the possible homolog assortments within one gamete.
choices.rationale: Fertilization combines two gametes but does not change the probability for a specified assortment in one gamete.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 1/8; crossing over in prophase I is required to create the 8 whole-chromosome assortments.
choices.rationale: The numerical probability is right, but the mechanism is wrong: independent orientation creates these combinations without crossing over.

title: linked-marker crossover inference
stem: Two linked markers are on one homolog as AB and on the other as ab. After meiosis, a researcher identifies gametes with AB, ab, Ab, and aB. Which gametes require an exchange between nonsister chromatids in the interval between the markers, and when can that exchange occur?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AB and ab; crossing over during prophase I is required to preserve the original combinations.
choices.rationale: Those are the parental marker combinations, which can be inherited without recombination.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ab and aB; crossing over between nonsister chromatids during prophase I can create these new combinations.
choices.rationale: Correct: The original chromosome arrangements are AB and ab. A crossover between the loci on nonsister chromatids during prophase I can exchange the second marker, producing Ab and aB. Independent separation alone preserves the linked arrangements.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ab and aB; separation of sister chromatids during meiosis II creates the new combinations without exchange.
choices.rationale: Sister-chromatid separation sorts existing chromatids; it does not exchange linked alleles between homologs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All four gamete classes; random fertilization creates their allele combinations inside a single gamete.
choices.rationale: Fertilization combines already formed gametes and cannot create new allele arrangements inside one gamete.

title: division-specific nondisjunction
stem: A diploid cell normally makes gametes with n=4 chromosomes. Four gametes from one meiosis have chromosome counts 5, 5, 3, and 3. Assuming a single nondisjunction event, which division failed, and how does the pattern support the inference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nondisjunction of sister chromatids in meiosis II; two gametes should still have 4 chromosomes.
choices.rationale: Meiosis II nondisjunction leaves two normal gametes, which are absent here.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Crossing over in prophase I; exchanging chromosome segments creates the count differences.
choices.rationale: Crossing over changes allele combinations, not the number of chromosomes in each gamete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nondisjunction of one homologous pair in meiosis I; all four gametes are abnormal, two n+1 and two n−1.
choices.rationale: Correct: Failure of homologs to separate in meiosis I puts both homologs in one daughter cell and neither in the other. Normal meiosis II then yields two 5-chromosome and two 3-chromosome gametes, matching all four observations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normal independent assortment; random orientation of homologs creates the count differences.
choices.rationale: Normal meiosis gives four n-chromosome gametes, not the observed two high and two low counts.

title: division-specific nondisjunction (variant 1)
stem: A diploid cell normally makes gametes with n=6 chromosomes. Four gametes from one meiosis have chromosome counts 6, 6, 7, and 5. Assuming a single nondisjunction event, which division failed, and how does the pattern support the inference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nondisjunction of homologous chromosomes in meiosis I; all four gametes should have abnormal counts.
choices.rationale: Meiosis I nondisjunction produces no normal gametes from that meiosis, but two are observed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Crossing over in prophase I; exchanging chromosome segments creates the count differences.
choices.rationale: Crossing over changes genetic combinations without this n±1 chromosome-count pattern.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal independent assortment; random orientation of homologs creates the count differences.
choices.rationale: Normal meiosis gives four n-chromosome gametes, not one high and one low count.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nondisjunction of sister chromatids in meiosis II; two gametes are normal and the others are n+1 and n−1.
choices.rationale: Correct: Normal homolog separation in meiosis I creates two n-chromosome cells. If sister chromatids fail to separate in one meiosis II cell, its gametes are 7 and 5; the other cell produces two normal 6-chromosome gametes.

title: division-specific nondisjunction (variant 3)
stem: A diploid organism normally makes gametes with n=10 chromosomes. One abnormal meiosis produced gametes with 10, 10, 11, and 9 chromosomes. If each gamete separately fuses with a normal 10-chromosome gamete, which zygote chromosome counts result, and which division most likely had one nondisjunction event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 20, 20, 21, and 19; a meiosis I homolog nondisjunction leaves two normal gametes.
choices.rationale: The zygote counts are right, but meiosis I nondisjunction would make all four gametes abnormal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 10, 10, 11, and 9; fertilization does not change chromosome number.
choices.rationale: The normal partner contributes 10 more chromosomes to each zygote.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 20, 20, 21, and 19; a meiosis II sister-chromatid nondisjunction leaves two normal gametes and one n+1/n−1 pair.
choices.rationale: Correct: Normal fertilization adds 10 chromosomes to each gamete, yielding 20, 20, 21, and 19. The two normal gametes and one high/low pair identify nondisjunction of sister chromatids in one meiosis II cell, not failure of homologs in meiosis I.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 21, 21, 19, and 19; meiosis II nondisjunction makes all four gametes abnormal.
choices.rationale: The two normal gametes rule out a single meiosis I nondisjunction and yield two normal 20-chromosome zygotes.
